faqSubtitle: Straight answers on replacing heavy dev tools, onboarding beginners, and keeping your configs safe.
faqLink5: Dev setup for beginners & vibe coding
faqQ1: Can Hearth replace Docker Desktop, Lens, Freelens, and DBngin?
faqA1: For daily local development, yes. Hearth sets up Colima on macOS (or native Docker Engine on Linux), provides a fast client-go Kubernetes UI, and runs local PostgreSQL, Redis, MySQL, and MongoDB servers with port-conflict detection. Keep your SQL client (TablePlus, DataGrip) and code editor.
faqQ2: I am new to coding or vibe coding with Claude Code / Cursor. Will Hearth help?
faqA2: Yes. Hearth includes a four-step New Computer setup wizard with Vibe Coding, Full-Stack Web, and Backend presets. It installs Git, Node, Python, Docker, and AI tools through official managers in the right order and verifies your PATH in a fresh shell so you never fight broken terminal scripts.
faqQ3: Does Hearth edit my ~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, or configs without asking?
faqA3: Never. Discovery is 100% read-only. Every change builds an explicit plan showing the exact commands and unified file diff first. Shell edits stay inside # >>> hearth >>> markers, create timestamped .bak backups, and comment out conflicting lines instead of deleting them.
faqQ4: How does Hearth work alongside Homebrew, mise, nvm, fnm, or WinGet?
faqA4: Hearth detects the manager that already owns each runtime or package and works through it rather than fighting it. If you use mise, fnm, Homebrew, uv, WinGet, Scoop, or APT, Hearth surfaces shadowed binaries and proposes fixes using your existing manager.
faqQ5: Why is Hearth so much lighter than Electron dev tools?
faqA5: Hearth is compiled to a single native Go binary using mygo (immediate-mode GPU UI) with zero Electron, zero Chromium, and zero embedded WebView. Downloads are ~13–19 MB (~44–48 MB installed) per architecture, with no bundled browser engine sitting in memory.
faqQ6: Is Hearth really free, open source, and offline-first?
faqA6: Yes. Hearth is MIT-licensed, free for personal and commercial teams, and runs 100% locally with zero accounts, zero cloud sync, and zero telemetry. Network access is only used when you explicitly download packages, check GitHub releases, or probe remote registries.
